result:
If there were a single lever to pull, it would be to eliminate the empathy gap—specifically, to give every human being the temporary, unmistakable ability to fully experience the internal reality of another person. 

Most of the world’s enduring catastrophes—war, systemic cruelty, exploitation, deep prejudice, and neglect—rely on abstraction. It is easy to harm, dismiss, or sacrifice people when their inner lives are theoretical, reduced to statistics, stereotypes, or political categories. 

If people could directly feel the grief, physical pain, fear, and quiet hopes of those affected by their decisions—whether across a dinner table, a border, or an economic divide—the cost of cruelty would become visceral and immediate rather than outsourced and ignored.

Technological progress, wealth creation, and political systems are powerful, but they are only amplifiers of human intent. Aligning that intent by making shared humanity impossible to deny would fundamentally reshape how every other problem—poverty, governance, conflict, ecology—is approached and solved.
